newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil refinery contract workers go on strike.
newsitem.headline: Brazil refinery contract workers go on strike.

text.p: Around 3,500 staff working for companies contracted by Brazil's largest refinery, Refinaria de Paulinia (Replan), in Sao Paulo state went on strike Tuesday, but the stoppage will not affect production, a refinery spokesman said.
He said the companies were contracted to build a coking unit within the refinery complex, which is due to come online in May 1998 and has no effect on current output levels.
"Even if the strike should continue for longer it will not affect output," the spokesman said.
The striking workers, employed by 23 different companies, are demanding a 35.58-percent pay rise to make up for inflation over the past two years.
Replan, the largest of 10 refineries belonging to state oil monopoly Petrobras', has capacity to process 327,000 barrels of oil per day.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
